data.hypothesis: On SM 8.0+, decomposing each signed 64-bit lane value into four 16-bit limbs permits four native 32-bit warp reductions instead of repeated 64-bit shuffle stages. Each limb sum over 32 lanes fits in int; valid intermediate totals remain within signed 64-bit bounds. The limb extraction and reconstruction may offset any instruction savings, so a full-call speedup is not assumed. Older architectures retain the existing 64-bit shuffle path.
data.notes: This is a distinct warp-reduction representation from the measured CUB and shared-warp-partial variants. Search measurements available here include the baseline at 46.4832 microseconds and the CUB trial 9ce980521a4545d5 at 29.9853 microseconds; neither is a repeated final confirmation. The controller should validate all required sizes and seeds, then compare repeated full-call measurements against the baseline. No performance result is claimed for this candidate.
transformations: Add an SM 8.0+ warp reduction that decomposes signed 64-bit lane values into four 16-bit limbs, reduces each limb with the existing int warp reduction, and reconstructs the exact lane-zero sum.

Use the new helper for both per-warp reduction stages; retain the pre-SM 8.0 64-bit shuffle fallback, four shared warp partials, single CTA barrier, recursive global passes, 128-thread mapping, and one input per lane.
